title: Cost of one ordered insertion
statement: Let $\alpha$ carry a linear order, and for $x \in \alpha$ and a list $\mathit{xs}$ over $\alpha$ let $\mathrm{insert}(x, \mathit{xs})$ denote the ordered insertion that scans $\mathit{xs}$ from the front, spending one unit of time on each element compared, until it reaches the first entry not smaller than $x$. Then the time cost incurred by $\mathrm{insert}(x, \mathit{xs})$ is at most the length of $\mathit{xs}$.
hypotheses_covered: x is an element of α
xs is a list over α
replaced: Inserting $x$ into a list $\mathit{xs}$ costs at most $\abs{\mathit{xs}}$ comparisons.
